title: the reflection object traversal adapters, one row per member
heading: ## Per-member rows: the class descriptor each of the reflection object traversal adapters loads (OPUS, 2026-10-03)
lead: The family `reflection object traversal adapters` (frontmatter: 304 members; {N} get a row here) shares two forms, stated here once and not repeated per row (the census row above). In 188 members (46 B), `lea rcx, [X]` comes first, then the flag selects one of two calls to the shared traversal `0063E2E0`, with `r8b` set to 1 or 0. In 116 members (75-76 B), the object pointer is offset by a constant member offset (`add rdx, 8`, or `inc rdx` in three members) and null-guarded, and each flag path then does `lea rcx, [X]` and calls `0063E2E0`. What differs from member to member is the class descriptor X its `lea rcx, [X]` loads (every load of it in the body names the same X). Each row anchors the first such `lea`, the member's distinguishing instruction, and states X and the class X describes. The class is read from the certified image: the static initialiser that does `lea rcx, [X]` and calls a descriptor-constructor wrapper, and that wrapper's `lea r8, [name]` before its one call to `00632D80`; every such initialiser must agree. {CHECK} re-derives every row and compares it with the committed {ROWS}. A member whose loads name more than one X, a descriptor not named by exactly one class, or a value that differs fails it. Two controls are refused: a swapped value and a moved anchor. Members that do not derive are listed in [`excluded.tsv`](../../_index/candidates/opus-ee-traversal-adapters-1003/excluded.tsv).
